# faucet-stream Matrix Machinery — Contract Map

Everything below is against repo root `/Users/c-sikawats/Documents/GitHub/Personal/faucet-stream`. The four focus files are large (config.rs 2150 lines, expand.rs 3033, executor.rs 3873); the structures and control flow you need are all in the first sections I quote below.

## 1. Verbatim struct definitions

### `MatrixRow` — `cli/src/config.rs:510-583`

```rust
/// One row of the `matrix:` block.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct MatrixRow {
    /// Row identifier. ... Anonymous rows get a synthetic `row-N` id.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub id: Option<String>,

    /// If set, this row runs once per record produced by the named parent row.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub parent: Option<String>,

    /// Row ids this row waits for. ... Pure completion-ordering — unlike
    /// `parent:`, no records are consumed and no per-record fan-out occurs.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub depends_on: Vec<String>,

    /// Dotted field path inside each parent record that uniquely identifies
    /// the record. Used as the state-key suffix. Default: `id`.
    #[serde(default = "default_parent_key")]
    pub parent_key: String,

    /// Partial override of `pipeline.source` (deep-merged).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub source: Option<PartialConnector>,

    /// Partial override of `pipeline.sink` (deep-merged).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub sink: Option<PartialConnector>,

    /// Row-level transforms. Appended after `T_pipeline` and `T_source` ...
    #[serde(default)]
    pub transforms: Option<Vec<TransformSpec>>,

    /// When `false`, drops upstream `T_pipeline` and `T_source` transforms
    /// for this row. Default `true`.
    #[serde(default = "default_true")]
    pub inherit_transforms: bool,

    /// If `Some`, replaces `pipeline.state` wholesale.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub state: Option<StateStoreSpec>,

    /// Matrix-row override semantics:
    /// - field absent  → `None`     — inherit from `pipeline.dlq`
    /// - `dlq: null`   → `Some(None)` — disable DLQ for this row
    /// - `dlq: { ... }` → `Some(Some(spec))` — replace base DLQ wholesale
    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = "deserialize_dlq_override")]
    pub dlq: Option<Option<DlqSpec>>,

    /// Per-row delivery override. `None` inherits the top-level `delivery`.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub delivery: Option<faucet_core::DeliveryMode>,

    /// Free-form classification tags for this row (#376). ...
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    pub tags: Vec<String>,

    /// Split this row into N independent invocations over a chunked range (#479) ...
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub partition: Option<crate::partition::PartitionSpec>,
}
```

Notes for your feature:
- `parent_key` default is `"id"` (`default_parent_key`, config.rs:1048).
- The row's `source`/`sink` are `Option<PartialConnector>` (config.rs:460-478), which carries `r#ref` (template name), `kind` (`type` override), `config` (deep-merge), and `status`. There is no `matrix` field on `MatrixRow` itself — the cross-product you want does not exist yet; a row is a single point, and fan-out today is only per-parent-record or per-partition-chunk.
- `PipelineConfig.matrix` is `Vec<MatrixRow>` at **config.rs:80** (`#[serde(default)]`; empty = one anonymous row). Topology mode (`pipeline.nodes`) is mutually exclusive with a non-empty `matrix` (config.rs:238-248).

### `ExpandedNode` — `cli/src/expand.rs:40-114`

```rust
/// One fully-merged matrix row, ready for the executor.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ExpandedNode {
    pub id: String,
    pub row_index: usize,
    pub role: NodeRole,
    pub source: ConnectorSpec,
    pub sink: ConnectorSpec,
    pub transforms: Vec<TransformSpec>,
    pub state: Option<StateStoreSpec>,
    /// Resolved DLQ spec for this row, or `None` if no DLQ applies.
    pub dlq: Option<crate::config::DlqSpec>,
    #[cfg(feature = "quality")]
    pub quality: Option<faucet_core::QualitySpec>,
    #[cfg(feature = "contract")]
    pub contract: Option<faucet_core::ContractSpec>,
    #[cfg(feature = "masking")]
    pub masking: Option<faucet_core::MaskingSpec>,
    /// The sink template name this node resolved (`sink.ref`, or `"default"`) ...
    pub sink_ref: String,
    /// Compiled schema-drift policy spec (pipeline-level; same for every node).
    pub schema: Option<faucet_core::SchemaDriftSpec>,
    /// Delivery guarantee for this row. ...
    pub delivery: faucet_core::DeliveryMode,
    /// The **derived** end-to-end guarantee this row's source × sink × config
    /// actually provides (issue #292) ...
    pub delivery_guarantee: faucet_core::DeliveryGuarantee,
    /// Row ids this node waits for (deduplicated, declaration order). ...
    pub depends_on: Vec<String>,
    /// Resolved readiness status for this row's source (#371) ...
    pub status: crate::config::SourceStatus,
    /// Effective classification tags (#376) = source-template `tags` ∪ row `tags` ...
    pub tags: Vec<String>,
    /// Every `${id.path}` placeholder that survived load-time interpolation. ...
    pub deferred_refs: Vec<DeferredRef>,
    /// A pre-built source that replaces the registry-built one for this node.
    /// Set only by `faucet dlq replay` (#281) ...
    pub source_override: Option<crate::dlq_replay::reader::SourceOverride>,
    /// Scoped-cleanup claim (#478) ...
    pub cleanup_scope: Option<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value>>,
}
```

Supporting enums/structs (expand.rs:116-132):

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum NodeRole {
    Root,
    Child { parent_id: String, parent_key: String },
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct DeferredRef {
    pub referenced_id: String,   // the `id` in ${id.path}
    pub dotted_path: String,     // the `path` in ${id.path}
    pub token: String,           // the literal `${id.path}` token text
}
```

`source_override` is the escape hatch already used to inject a pre-built source (DLQ replay); your discovery feature could reuse the same idea if you need to substitute a runtime-built source.

## 2. How a `parent:` child gets its N invocations at runtime

The whole runtime lives in `run_expanded()` — **executor.rs:216-568** — which runs **level-by-level** (roots = level 0), not a recursive walk.

Data structures:
- `CapturedRecords = Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, Vec<Arc<Value>>>>>` — **executor.rs:46**. Keyed by node id; holds each parent's emitted records as `Arc<Value>` (pointer-clone hand-off, #160).
- A parent's records are captured by wrapping its sink in a `CapturingSink` (constructed in `run_one_invocation`, executor.rs:1088-1096) and, on success, appended to the map in `run_unit` (**executor.rs:606-617**): `.extend(records.into_iter().map(Arc::new))`. Capture only happens when `capture.is_some()`, i.e. the node has children (see `build_projections`).
- Only the referenced fields are kept: `build_projections()` (**executor.rs:778-817**) computes a `Projection::Full` or `Projection::Paths(...)` per parent from each child's `parent_key` plus its `deferred_refs`. Applied via `project_record` (executor.rs:759).

Per-level fan-out (**executor.rs:334-424**):
1. `ready` = every remaining node whose parent and all `depends_on` are terminal (executor.rs:290-308).
2. `level_records` drains the consumed parents' records out of the shared map (executor.rs:334-347).
3. For a `NodeRole::Child`, it fetches `parent_records = level_records.get(parent_id)` and loops over **each record**, building one `Unit` per record (**executor.rs:387-423**). Empty parent output → child skipped (executor.rs:392-398).

The per-record context map passed to interpolation is built in **`run_one_invocation`, executor.rs:1037-1044**:

```rust
if let (Some(record), NodeRole::Child { parent_id, .. }) = (parent_record, &node.role) {
    let ctx: HashMap<String, Value> = HashMap::from([(parent_id.clone(), record.clone())]);
    resolve_inplace(&mut source_cfg, &ctx)?;
    resolve_inplace(&mut sink_cfg, &ctx)?;
    if let Some(scope) = cleanup_scope.as_mut() {
        resolve_inplace(scope, &ctx)?;
    }
}
```

So the ctx map shape is `{ parent_id => full_parent_record_json }` — a single entry keyed by the parent's row id. `resolve_inplace` (a local helper in executor.rs that walks strings calling `interpolate_record`) is what expands `${parent_id.dotted.path}` per record. Note `${now.*}` is resolved *before* this, on every invocation, via `resolve_now_inplace` (executor.rs:1015-1016).

Concurrency model (executor.rs:444-461): all units of a level are spawned into a `tokio::task::JoinSet`; each task first `sem.acquire().await` on a shared `Arc<Semaphore>` (executor.rs:228, size `max_concurrent` = config or `default_concurrency()` clamped 1..=8, executor.rs:207-212). Roots and children share the one budget.

## 3. Per-invocation state key + `build_state_key`

**executor.rs:641-651**:

```rust
/// Produce `{pipeline_name}::{row_id}` or `{pipeline_name}::{row_id}::{key}`.
pub(crate) fn build_state_key(
    pipeline_name: &str,
    row_id: &str,
    parent_key: Option<&str>,
) -> String {
    match parent_key {
        None => format!("{pipeline_name}::{row_id}"),
        Some(k) => format!("{pipeline_name}::{row_id}::{k}"),
    }
}
```

Callers:
- Root: `build_state_key(&opts.pipeline_name, &node.id, None)` — **executor.rs:378**.
- Child: **executor.rs:402-422**. For each parent record it computes `pk_value = resolve_parent_key(record, parent_key)` (executor.rs:671-681, dotted-path walk) then `pk_string = value_to_string_brief(...)` (falls back to `"(missing)"`), then `build_state_key(&opts.pipeline_name, &node.id, Some(&pk_string))`. So the child key is `{name}::{row}::{parent_record_key}`.
- Collision guard: siblings sharing a parent are checked into a `seen_keys` set; a repeat is `CliError::DuplicateStateKey` (executor.rs:411-416).
- `validate_unit_state_key` (executor.rs:657-668) validates the key up front only when `uses_state`.

There is a further shard suffix in `run_one_invocation`: `effective_state_key = format!("{state_key}::{}", shard.id)` (executor.rs:1208-1211), and partitioned rows carry a `::partition::{chunk}` suffix baked into the node id at expand time (expand.rs:1033).

`StateKeyOverride` — **executor.rs:1212-1219** — wraps the built source so the executor's per-row key overrides the source's natural (kind-shared) key:

```rust
let source: Box<dyn Source> = if state.is_some() && source.state_key().is_some() {
    Box::new(StateKeyOverride { inner: source, key: effective_state_key })
} else {
    source
};
```

## 4. RESERVED_IDS and reserved interpolation-id prefixes

`RESERVED_IDS` — **expand.rs:27-37**:

```rust
pub const RESERVED_IDS: &[&str] = &[
    "env", "file", "secret", "matrix", "pipeline",
    "now", "backfill", "param", "partition",
];
```

Enforced on row ids at **expand.rs:307-309** (`CliError::ReservedRowId`). Duplicate ids → `DuplicateRowId` (expand.rs:310-313).

Reserved runtime/deferred interpolation ids (not parent-record refs) are handled specially in three places:
- **`check_refs`** (expand.rs:1122-1159) is where an unknown `${id.path}` is rejected. It uses `iter_directives` + `classify_directive` (interpolate.rs). For a `Directive::Deferred { id, .. }`: `param` → hard error (never-bound, expand.rs:1135-1144); otherwise if `id != "now" && id != "backfill" && id != "partition" && !id_set.contains(id)` → `CliError::UnknownInterpolationId` (expand.rs:1145-1155). `env`/`file`/`secret` never reach here because with a colon they classify as `LoadTime` and are already resolved.
- `check_refs` is called over every row's source/sink config and the pipeline-level source/sink/sources/sinks (expand.rs:370-394).
- `collect_deferred` (expand.rs:1220-1240) skips `now`/`backfill`/`partition` so they aren't treated as parent-record deps; everything else becomes a `DeferredRef`.
- `reject_runtime_tokens` (expand.rs:1168-1181) rejects *any* deferred token in transform/state/dlq configs — runtime `${...}` tokens are only legal in source/sink configs.

The classification rule itself is `classify_directive` — **interpolate.rs:250-258**: colon → `LoadTime { prefix, body }`; else split on first `.` → `Deferred { id, path }`.

## 5. Where a runtime "run a source, project a field, dedup" step hooks in

Two existing precedents build+run a source with **no sink** — both are your best hook models:

1. **`faucet discover`** — `cli/src/commands/discover.rs` (this is the closest existing thing to your feature, issue #211). `run()` at discover.rs:19-110 does: `build_source(&spec.kind, spec.config.clone(), &auth, None)` (discover.rs:39-40), checks `source.supports_discover()`, then `source.discover().await` to enumerate datasets, filters them (`filter_datasets`), and **generates a config with one matrix row per dataset** (`render_discovered_config`, discover.rs:80). That is fan-out over discovered values, but resolved *ahead of run* into static rows, not at runtime.

2. **`faucet preview`** — `cli/src/commands/preview.rs:54-77`: `build_source(...)` then `let records = source.fetch_all().await?;`, applies transform stages, takes `args.limit`, prints. No sink.

3. **`reconcile::run`** — `cli/src/reconcile.rs:123-139`: the canonical minimal "build a source, drain it, extract a field" pattern:

```rust
let source = crate::registry::build_source(&spec.count.kind, spec.count.config.clone(), auth, None).await?;
let records = source.fetch_all().await?;
let authoritative = extract_count(&records, spec.count.count_field.as_deref())?;
```

The underlying primitive is the `Source` trait — `crates/core/src/traits.rs:12-48`:
- `fetch_with_context(&self, context: &HashMap<String, Value>)` (traits.rs:20) — the primary method; **this is exactly the context-map contract your discovery step could feed**, same shape as the executor's per-record `ctx`.
- `fetch_all(&self)` (traits.rs:26) — convenience with empty context.
- `stream_pages(...)` (traits.rs:73) for paged draining.

Field projection uses `resolve_dotted(root, path)` (interpolate.rs:328-344), and the executor's `resolve_parent_key` / `walk_value` (executor.rs:671-681, 720-730) are the dotted-path readers you'd mirror. There is **no existing dedup helper** — you would add that.

Assessment: the executor does *not* currently have a runtime "enumerate a value-set from a source then fan out rows over it" step. The per-parent-record fan-out (executor.rs:387-423) is the structural analog: it takes a `Vec<Arc<Value>>` and emits one Unit per element. A discovery-driven matrix would most naturally either (a) resolve to static rows before the run like `discover` does, or (b) introduce a new pre-level in `run_expanded` that runs discovery sources (via `build_source` + `fetch_all`), projects+dedups values, and synthesizes `Unit`s the way the child branch does — feeding the cross-product into the same `ctx` map / `build_state_key` machinery. The Unit-per-element loop and `CapturedRecords` are your templates; a cross-product would multiply several such value-sets before building units.

## 6. How `depends_on` completion-ordering interacts with `parent:`

They are **orthogonal and combinable** — a node can have both.

- **Expand-time**: `parent` and `depends_on` are validated independently. Parents: single-parent-chain cycle check `detect_cycle` (expand.rs:1045-1065). `depends_on`: unknown-dep / self-dep checks + per-row dedup preserving order (expand.rs:343-364). Then the **combined** graph is checked with **Kahn's algorithm** in `detect_combined_cycle` (**expand.rs:1073-1117**): for each row, `prereqs = parent (if any) ∪ depends_on`, computes in-degrees, topo-sorts; any unprocessed node → `CliError::DependencyCycle`. This is why a cycle routed *through* a `depends_on` edge can't deadlock the executor.
- The BFS `order` that `expand()` emits (expand.rs:410-418) is built from the **parent** graph only (roots first, then children breadth-first) — `depends_on` does **not** affect emission order; it is enforced purely at runtime.
- **Runtime readiness** (`run_expanded`, **executor.rs:290-308**): a node is `ready` only when BOTH hold:
  - parent is terminal: `Root => true`, else `completed.contains(parent_id) || skipped_subtrees.contains(parent_id)`;
  - AND `node.depends_on.iter().all(|d| completed.contains(d) || skipped_subtrees.contains(d))`.
- **Difference in semantics**: `parent:` hands off records (the child fans out once per parent record, consuming `level_records`); `depends_on:` is pure completion-ordering — no records consumed, no fan-out (see the module doc, executor.rs:13-17, and `MatrixRow.depends_on` doc, config.rs:522-527).
- **Skip cascade**: if a parent failed/was skipped, the child subtree is skipped (executor.rs:352-358); if any `depends_on` prerequisite failed/was skipped, the node is skipped too (executor.rs:363-374). Both cascade into `skipped_subtrees`. Readiness only asks "is there anything left to wait for"; whether a terminal prereq *skips* the node is decided in the unit loop.

A node with both `parent: p` and `depends_on: [d]` therefore fans out per record of `p` **and** waits for `d` to fully complete first; readiness requires both terminal, and a failure of either skips it.

# Discovery-driven request matrix (#501): fan a stream out over the CROSS
# PRODUCT of value-sets enumerated from live discovery calls at run time —
# "sync this report once per {subsidiary} × {custom-field}".
#
#   faucet validate cli/examples/discovery_matrix.yaml
#
# A `discover:` row runs its source once, projects `select` from each record,
# dedups, and publishes the value-set under `as`. A `for_each: [dims]` row then
# runs once per tuple of the cartesian product, with `${dim.alias}` substituted
# into the source URL and sink path. Discovery + fan-out rows share one
# `pipeline.sources` template (the `ref` path) and override only the deltas.
version: 1
name: reports_by_subsidiary_and_field

pipeline:
  # One complete REST template both the discovery calls and the report fan-out
  # reference — same auth / base_url, different path per row.
  sources:
    api:
      type: rest
      config:
        method: GET
        base_url: https://api.example.com
        path: /
        auth:
          type: bearer
          config:
            token: ${env:API_TOKEN}
        query_params: {}
        pagination: { type: None }
        replication_method: { type: FullTable }

  sink:
    type: jsonl
    config:
      path: ./out/report-${subsidiaries.subsidiary_id}-${fields.field_id}.jsonl

matrix:
  # ── Discovery dimensions (run once each, deduped, cached) ──
  - id: subsidiaries
    discover:
      source:
        ref: api
        config: { path: /subsidiaries, records_path: "$.subsidiaries[*]" }
      select: "$.id"
      as: subsidiary_id

  - id: fields
    discover:
      source:
        ref: api
        config: { path: /custom-fields, records_path: "$.fields[*]" }
      select: "$.id"
      as: field_id

  # ── Fan-out: one invocation per (subsidiary × field) tuple ──
  - id: trial_balance
    for_each: [subsidiaries, fields]
    source:
      ref: api
      config:
        path: /reports/trial-balance
        records_path: "$.rows[*]"
        query_params:

### `discover:` / `for_each:` — discovery-driven fan-out (#501)

A `discover:` row enumerates a **value-set at run time** from a live endpoint,
and a `for_each:` row fans a stream out over the **cartesian product** of those
value-sets — "sync this report once per `{subsidiary} × {custom-field}`
returned by a discovery call". This is the first-class version of the
"enumerate then fan out" shape common to report-style APIs.

```yaml
pipeline:
  sources:
    api:                      # one complete template both roles reference
      type: rest
      config: { method: GET, base_url: "https://api.example.com", path: "/", auth: { type: none },
                query_params: {}, pagination: { type: None }, replication_method: { type: FullTable } }
  sink: { type: jsonl, config: { path: "./out/${subs.subsidiary_id}-${flds.field_id}.jsonl" } }

matrix:
  - id: subs                  # discovery dimension
    discover:
      source: { ref: api, config: { path: "/subsidiaries", records_path: "$.subsidiaries[*]" } }
      select: "$.id"          # JSONPath projecting the value from each record
      as: subsidiary_id       # exposed as ${subs.subsidiary_id}
  - id: flds
    discover:
      source: { ref: api, config: { path: "/fields", records_path: "$.fields[*]" } }
      select: "$.id"
      as: field_id
  - id: report                # runs once per (subsidiary × field) tuple
    for_each: [subs, flds]
    source:
      ref: api
      config:
        path: "/reports/trial-balance"
        records_path: "$.rows[*]"
        query_params: { subsidiary_id: "${subs.subsidiary_id}", field_id: "${flds.field_id}" }
```

Semantics:

- A **`discover:` row** runs its source once, projects `select` (a dot-path,
  optionally `$`-prefixed; `$` = whole record) from each record, and **dedups**
  (first-seen order; null / missing values skipped). It has **no sink** and
  writes nothing. It runs once per pipeline run, cached across all dependents.
- The discovery `source` is either a `{ ref: <name> }` to a `pipeline.sources`
  template (recommended — reuses a complete connector config) or a standalone
  `{ type, config }`. It is **not** merged over the `default` template.
- A **`for_each: [dims]` row** runs once per tuple of the cartesian product of
  the listed dimensions, with `${<dim>.<alias>}` substituted into its source
  and sink config. Time windows (`${now.*}`, `faucet backfill`) compose
  per-invocation without multiplying the matrix.
- Each dimension is folded into the row's `depends_on`, so readiness, the skip
  cascade, and cycle detection reuse the ordering machinery. Per-tuple state
  keys (`{name}::{row}::alias=value&…`) let every cell resume independently.
- Guards (all at load time via `faucet validate`): `for_each` must name
  `discover:` rows; a `discover:` row can't carry a sink, `parent:`, or
  `for_each:`; `for_each` can't combine with `parent:` (v1). The product is
  bounded by `MAX_MATRIX_PRODUCT` (10 000) — a larger cross-product fails
  rather than spawning an unbounded fleet.

See `cli/examples/discovery_matrix.yaml`.

Closes #501.

## What

Adds a **discovery-driven request matrix**: a `discover:` row enumerates a value-set at run time, and a `for_each: [dims]` row fans a stream out over the **cartesian product** of those dimensions — one invocation per tuple, with `${dim.alias}` substituted into the source/sink config. This is the first-class "enumerate then fan out" shape report-style APIs need (rillet: subsidiary × custom-field × month; Dynamics 365 BC: entity per company).

```yaml
matrix:
  - id: subs
    discover:
      source: { ref: api, config: { path: /subsidiaries, records_path: "$.subsidiaries[*]" } }
      select: "$.id"
      as: subsidiary_id
  - id: fields
    discover:
      source: { ref: api, config: { path: /custom-fields, records_path: "$.fields[*]" } }
      select: "$.id"
      as: field_id
  - id: trial_balance
    for_each: [subs, fields]        # |subs| × |fields| invocations
    source:
      ref: api
      config:
        path: /reports/trial-balance
        query_params: { subsidiary_id: "${subs.subsidiary_id}", field_id: "${fields.field_id}" }
```

## Design

- **`discovery_matrix` module** holds the pure planning logic — projection + dedup, cartesian product, per-tuple interpolation context, tuple state-key suffix — fully unit-tested (the acceptance criterion).
- **`NodeRole::Discovery` / `Product`** extend the executor. `for_each` dims are folded into `depends_on`, so readiness, the skip-cascade, and cycle detection all reuse the existing machinery — only the fan-out branch is new. `Unit` carries a multi-key product context resolved through the same `interpolate_record` path as parent/child. Discovery runs source-only via `run_discovery` (no sink).
- **Discovery source** is a `{ ref }` to a `pipeline.sources` template (recommended — reuses a complete connector config) or a standalone `{ type, config }`; it is **not** merged over the `default` template (which carries `${dim}` tokens meant for the fan-out rows — that would self-reference the enumeration).
- **Composition**: `${now.*}` / `faucet backfill` windows stay per-invocation, so "month × subsidiary × field" is a date window over the discovery cross-product for free.
- **Guards** (load-time, via `faucet validate`): `for_each` must name `discover:` rows; a discovery row has no sink and can't be `parent:`/`for_each:`; `for_each` + `parent:` is rejected (v1); the product is bounded by `MAX_MATRIX_PRODUCT` (10 000).

## Tests / docs

- Pure unit tests (projection/dedup/cartesian/product-size/state-key), expand-time validation + role assignment + `ref`-template resolution, and wiremock end-to-end (single dimension, two-dimension cross-product, empty-discovery skip). No regressions in the existing executor/expand suites.
- Committed config JSON schema (`MatrixRow.discover`/`for_each` + `DiscoverSpec`), `docs/book/src/reference/config.md`, `cli/README.md`, and a runnable `cli/examples/discovery_matrix.yaml`.

      variant: z3z1ma

      config:

          add_underscore_when_invalid: true

=== bigquery-config.py (head) ===
import os
import yaml

provider_dir = os.getenv("PROVIDER_DIR")
if not provider_dir:
    raise ValueError("PROVIDER_DIR environment variable is required")

meltano_file = os.path.join(provider_dir, "meltano.yml")

# Read existing meltano.yml
with open(meltano_file, "r") as f:
    meltano_config = yaml.safe_load(f)

# Get bigquery config values from env
upsert = os.getenv("BIGQUERY_UPSERT")
overwrite = os.getenv("BIGQUERY_OVERWRITE")
target_name = os.getenv("TARGET_NAME", "target-bigquery")

# Update bigquery config if env vars are set
if upsert is not None or overwrite is not None:
    config = next(
        (loader["config"]
        for loader in meltano_config["plugins"]["loaders"]
        if loader["name"] == target_name),
        None,
    )
    if config is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Loader '{target_name}' not found in meltano.yml — cannot update BigQuery config.")

    # Update config values
    if upsert is not None:
        print("Replacing upsert with: ", upsert)
        config["upsert"] = upsert.lower() == "true"
    if overwrite is not None:
        print("Replacing overwrite with: ", overwrite)
        config["overwrite"] = overwrite.lower() == "true"

    if config.get("upsert") is True and config.get("overwrite") is True:
        raise ValueError("BIGQUERY_UPSERT and BIGQUERY_OVERWRITE are mutually exclusive — both cannot be true simultaneously.")

## Meltano tap mechanism analysis (DrivetrainAi)

All six are custom DrivetrainAi taps built on the Singer SDK, run under Meltano, loading to `target-bigquery` (z3z1ma). Stream selection is via a `streams_to_discover`/`streams_to_sync` CSV in every tap. Files cited are under `g3/<name>/tap_<name>/` unless noted.

---

### RILLET (ERP / accounting close software)
- **Mechanism:** REST-JSON to `https://api.rillet.com`, Singer SDK `RESTStream`. Report endpoints pin header `X-Rillet-API-Version: 3`. (`streams.py`, `tap.py`)
- **Auth:** Bearer static token (`auth_token`) via `BearerTokenAuthenticator`. (`streams.py:221-224`)
- **Pagination:** cursor-in-body — `$.pagination.next_cursor` → `cursor` query param, `limit=100`. Report streams are single-response (`next_page_token_jsonpath = None`). (`streams.py:205,236-242`)
- **Streams (static classes, filtered by `streams_to_sync`):** two families.
  - *Collection streams* (append-ish, cursor-paged): account, bank_account, bill, book_period, credit_memo, customer, field, invoice, journal_entry, organization, product, subsidiary, vendor, journal_entry_report.
  - *Report streams* — the parity-heavy part, driven by the SDK `partitions` property (each partition = one API call), NOT parent-child streams:
    - **balance_sheet_report** (`/reports/balance-sheet`): partitions = **month-end dates** from `start_date` to today (`_iter_month_ends`); each call `breakdown_by=SUBSIDIARY`. (`streams.py:724-740`)
    - **income_statement_report / cash_flow_statement_report** (`_PeriodReportStream`): partitions = **(month-window) × (breakdown_spec)**. Windows are first→last-of-month `(from_date,to_date)` via `_iter_month_ranges`; breakdown_specs = one `SUBSIDIARY` call **plus one `CUSTOM_FIELD` call per custom-field id**, where field ids are fetched on-the-fly by paginating `/fields` (`_fetch_collection_ids`, cached). CUSTOM_FIELD requires an extra `custom_field_id` query param. (`streams.py:755-866`)
    - **trial_balance_report** (`/reports/trial-balance`): partitions = **month-window × subsidiary_id**. Subsidiary id list = **union of `/subsidiaries` and the SUBSIDIARY breakdowns pulled from a live `/reports/balance-sheet` call** (`_fetch_subsidiary_breakdown_ids`) — the breakdown source adds intercompany *elimination entities* that `/subsidiaries` omits (ENG-81840; without them the summed TB doesn't reconcile to the BS). Falls back to a single consolidated call (`subsidiary_id=None`) if no subsidiaries. (`streams.py:869-958`)
- **Incremental:** none — no `replication_key`. Full re-pull every run bounded only by `start_date` month iteration; `target-bigquery` is `overwrite: true`.
- **Record shaping (heavy):** `flatten_dict` on every row; `unnest_list_config` explodes nested line-item arrays into child rows (bill/credit_memo/invoice/journal_entry `items`, field `values`) with composite PKs like `[id, item_id]`. Report parsers **flatten the entire report tree** by hand: recursive `_walk_balance_sheet_tree` / `_walk_sections` emit one leaf row per (account × subsidiary breakdown), denormalizing section/group/subgroup totals onto each row, dropping consolidated row-totals, and synthesizing "rolled-up" Cash lines from subgroup totals where Rillet hides bank accounts (`_is_rolled_up_leaf`). `item_fields` JSON-stringified. Custom 429 handling (constant 65s backoff, no Retry-After header).
- **Parity risk: VERY HIGH.** The report fan-out (month windows × subsidiaries × custom-fields), the on-the-fly id discovery via extra un-paginated helper calls, the elimination-entity union, and the hand-rolled hierarchical report-tree flattening with reconciliation-specific rules are all bespoke tap logic with no generic-connector equivalent.

---

### STRIPE (payments)
- **Mechanism:** **Vendor SDK** — the official `stripe` Python SDK (`sdk_object.list()`, `stripe.Charge`/`Invoice`/etc. in `constants.SDK_OBJECTS`) for entity streams. Plus a **separate Reporting-API path** (`reportbase.py`) using raw `requests` against `https://api.stripe.com/v1/reporting`. (`base.py:206-213`, `reportbase.py`)
- **Auth:** API key. SDK path sets `stripe.api_key`; report path uses HTTP Basic (`api_key` as user). Org keys (`sk_org_live_*`) add a `Stripe-Context` header (+ pinned `Stripe-Version: 2023-10-16`). (`base.py:228-231`, `reportbase.py:550-576`)
- **Pagination:** SDK path — manual cursor loop via `starting_after=last.id` + `has_more` (re-issues full params each page so the org context header survives). Report path — issue report run → poll download URL → stream CSV. (`base.py:363-380`, `reportbase.py:642-828`)
- **Streams (static):** ~23 entity streams (accounts, charges, invoices, customers, subscriptions, payouts, refunds, disputes, credit_notes, balance_transactions, etc.) + **subscription_history** + one **report stream** `card_payments_fees_transaction_level_1` (report_type `card_payments_fees.transaction_level.1`).
- **Incremental:** two modes. `is_immutable=True` streams replicate on `created` directly. Mutable streams (checkout_sessions, discounts, subscriptions, subscription_history) replicate via the **Stripe Events API** — `sdk_object = stripe.Event` filtered by `EVENT_TYPE_FILTERS` type globs, unwrapping `data.object`. Bookmark key `created` (or `date`). Time window is **chunked into half-month slices** and fetched with a `ThreadPoolExecutor` (`max_workers`, default 9); disputes use a 90-day lookback + 90-day chunks. Event streams **dedupe by object id** (latest-created wins) to avoid MERGE conflicts. (`base.py:185-494`)
- **Record shaping:** `flatten_keys` (dict → `key_subkey`, nested → JSON string), `string_keys` (JSON-stringify), event `record_path` unwrap, extra `created`/`event_id` keys. Report path parses CSV rows to dicts. (`base.py:299-345`)
- **Parity risk: HIGH.** Reliance on the official Stripe SDK, the Events-API-as-incremental model with dedup, threaded month-chunk fetching, and the async report-run/poll/CSV-download flow.

---

### HUBSPOT (CRM)
- **Mechanism:** REST-JSON, HubSpot CRM v3. Core object reads via **POST `/crm/v3/objects/{type}/search`** (search endpoint), plus `/crm/v3/properties/{type}` (schema), `/crm/v3/schemas` (custom-object resolution), `/crm/v3/objects/{type}/batch/read`, `/crm/v3/lists/{id}/memberships`. Raw `requests` via `utils/req.py` (SDK `_request` is monkey-patched to route POST search through it). (`streams/object.py:278-280,720-735`)
- **Auth:** **OAuth2 refresh-token** flow — exchanges `client_id`/`client_secret`/`refresh_token` at `https://api.hubspot.com/oauth/v1/token`, caches access token with 10-min buffer. (`auth.py`)
- **Pagination:** cursor-in-body — search `paging.next.after` → payload `after`; **`limit:200`, sorted by id ASC**, with an id-filter workaround (`hs_object_id GT last_id`) to break past the search API's hard 10k-result cap. (`streams/object.py:362-436,783-791`)
- **Streams (heavily discovered/dynamic):** `tap.py::discover_streams` runs a multi-pass matcher over the requested names against object/association/user/history/analytics registries, then dynamically synthesizes classes for: **list-membership streams** (`list_<id>`), **custom objects** (resolved by name against `/crm/v3/schemas`, e.g. `agreement`→`p21230183_agreement`), **custom-object property-history** (`<obj>_property_history`), and **custom associations** (`<from>_to_<to>`), building `type(...)` subclasses at runtime and wiring `parent_stream_type`.
- **Parent→child fan-out:** object streams accumulate ids across `child_batch_pages` (default 5) then dispatch child association/history streams **concurrently** (`ThreadPoolExecutor`, `sibling_child_workers=3`) via `/batch/read` (sub-batched 200, 5 workers). Deals fan out to deal_company/deal_contact/deal_property_history/merged deals. (`streams/object.py:197-276,523-551`)
- **Incremental:** search filter `hs_lastmodifieddate GTE` bookmark; also pulls **archived** records separately (GET list, or ID-enumerate + batch/read when >250 properties). (`streams/object.py:365-436,553-604`)
- **Record shaping:** the `properties` bag is popped and flattened to `property_<name>` columns (raw bag dropped to halve BQ size); string-"true"/"false"→bool coercion; epoch-ms→ISO date coercion for date-typed props; `schema_override` renames. **Notably the tap issues BigQuery DELETE-before-emit for association children** (tap reaches into the warehouse directly). (`streams/object.py:470-521`; `utils/bigquery.py`)
- **Parity risk: VERY HIGH.** POST-search cursor-in-body + 10k id-filter workaround, runtime class synthesis for custom objects/associations/history, concurrent parent→child batch-read fan-out, archived-record second pass, and the direct-to-BigQuery DELETE side-channel all far exceed a declarative REST connector.

---

### RAMP (corporate cards / spend)
- **Mechanism:** REST-JSON to `https://api.ramp.com/developer/v1`, Singer SDK `RESTStream` (`meltano_utils.DriveRestStream` indirectly). (`base.py`, `constants.py`)
- **Auth:** **OAuth2 client_credentials** — POST to `/token` with HTTP Basic (`client_id`/`client_secret`) + space-separated `scopes` (large default scope list in `tap.py`); token cached with 5-min refresh buffer, shared across all streams. (`auth.py`)
- **Pagination:** HATEOAS — full next-page URL under `page.next` (`BaseHATEOASPaginator`), `page_size=100`; single-object streams use `SinglePagePaginator`. (`base.py:8-14,44-54`)
- **Streams (static, ~22):** business, business_balance, entities, bills, bill_drafts, cards, departments, limits, locations, merchants, purchase_orders, receipts, reimbursements, spend_programs, transactions, users, vendors, statements, transfers, repayments, cashbacks, accounts, balance_history. `business`/`business_balance` are single-object. (`streams.py`)
- **Incremental:** none (no `replication_key`); server-side date filters only on first-page params: transactions/reimbursements `from_date`, bills `from_created_at` (from config `start_date`). BQ loader `overwrite: true`. (`streams.py:91-95,200-204,236-240`)
- **Record shaping:** per-stream `convert_to_string` JSON-stringifies nested fields (`stringify_complex_fields`) for flat BQ columns. (`base.py:56-57`)
- **Parity risk: LOW.** Straightforward paginated REST + OAuth2 client-credentials + per-stream date filter; maps cleanly to a generic REST source.

---

### BREX (corporate cards / spend)
- **Mechanism:** REST-JSON to `https://platform.brexapis.com`, Singer SDK `RESTStream` (`DriveRestStream`). (`base.py`)
- **Auth:** **static API key** as Bearer header (`APIKeyAuthenticator`, `Authorization: Bearer {api_key}`). No token exchange. (`base.py:38-46`)
- **Pagination:** cursor-in-body — `next_cursor` in response → `cursor` query param, `limit` up to 1000, records at `$.items[*]`. (`base.py:8-20,49-70`)
- **Streams (static, 6):** users (`/v2/users`), cards (`/v2/cards`), departments (`/v2/departments`), expenses (`/v1/expenses`), primary_card_account_transaction (`/v2/transactions/card/primary`), vendors (`/v1/vendors`). (`streams.py`)
- **Incremental:** none (no `replication_key`); full pull, BQ `overwrite: true`.
- **Record shaping:** `expand[]` query params to hydrate related objects (e.g. expenses expand location/department/merchant/user/budget/payment), `flatten_keys` (dict→`key_subkey`), `convert_to_string` (JSON-stringify). (`base.py:71-90`, `streams.py`)
- **Parity risk: LOW.** Clean cursor-paged REST with Bearer key; the only nuance is `expand[]` array query params.

---

### PLAID (bank-account aggregation)
- **Mechanism:** REST-JSON, **POST-only** to `https://{sandbox|production}.plaid.com` (env-dependent host). Uses raw `requests` via `DriveRestStream` — **NOT** the Plaid vendor SDK, despite the "Plaid" keyword in pyproject. `Plaid-Version` header pinned (default `2020-09-14`). (`base.py:118-165`)
- **Auth:** credentials in the **request body** (`client_id` + `secret` + per-Item `access_token`), not headers. Access token is resolved by `item_id` at request time and deliberately kept out of partition context/STATE/logs. (`base.py:190-233`)
- **Pagination:** cursor. transactions use `/transactions/sync`'s `has_more`+`next_cursor` (`PlaidSyncPaginator`); accounts are single-shot. (`streams.py:64-92`)
- **Streams (static, 2):** accounts (`POST /accounts/get`), transactions (`POST /transactions/sync`).
- **Plaid Item / access-token model:** one **partition per linked bank (Item)**. Config carries a single scalar `access_token`+`item_id` (a connection instance = one Item), wrapped into a one-element internal list; a deprecated `access_tokens` JSON-array fallback still supports multi-Item. STATE is partitioned by `item_id` (`state_partitioning_keys=["item_id"]`). (`base.py:60-165`, `streams.py`)
- **Incremental:** transactions use Plaid's **cursor sync** (not a timestamp key) — first run per Item = no cursor → full history; cursor saved to STATE **per page** (resumable mid-run); later runs send saved cursor for deltas. Emits `added`+`modified`; `removed` is logged but **not propagated** (upsert loader doesn't hard-delete — an explicit soft-delete gap). accounts are full-refresh (balances snapshot). `start_date` filter applied only on the first full run. (`streams.py:94-260`)
- **Record shaping:** flatten `balances`→`balances_*`, JSON-stringify nested txn fields (location, payment_meta, personal_finance_category, counterparties, category), stamp `item_id`/`institution_name`, composite PKs `[transaction_id,item_id]`/`[account_id,item_id]`. Fatal-vs-retriable Plaid error-code classification. (`base.py:8-20,254-296`, `streams.py`)
- **Parity risk: MEDIUM-HIGH.** POST-body auth, the per-Item partition + access-token-by-item_id resolution, the cursor-sync incremental model with per-page STATE, and the unhandled `removed`/soft-delete gap are all Plaid-specific behaviors a generic REST source won't cover.

---

**Cross-cutting notes:** every tap does record shaping to flatten nested JSON into BQ-friendly flat string columns (either the tap's own `flatten_dict`/`convert_to_string`/`flatten_keys` or Singer post_process). Rillet and HubSpot are the two extreme parity risks (bespoke report-tree fan-out; runtime-synthesized discovered streams + direct-BQ side effects). Ramp and Brex are the cleanest. Stripe's vendor-SDK + Events-API-incremental + async report path is a distinct mechanism class. Plaid's item/access-token model is its defining complexity. The `meltano_taps/` clone was left intact.</result>

# PART B — Sink: DrivetrainAi/target-bigquery (z3z1ma fork)

Effective config: `denormalized: true`, `method: batch_job`, `schema_resolver_version: "2"`, `column_name_transforms.add_underscore_when_invalid: true`, `cluster_on_key_properties: true`. Anthropic: `batch_size: 10000`, `upsert:[messages_usage,cost_report,api_key_costs,claude_code_usage]` + `overwrite:[api_keys,users,workspaces]` (disjoint). OpenAI: `batch_size: 10000`, `overwrite: true` (all streams). (The `batch_size: 5000` in the task prompt is not what the committed configs use.) Sink class resolved by `target.py:get_sink_class` → **`BigQueryBatchJobDenormalizedSink`** (`batch_job.py:137`).

## Table naming — `core.py:table_name` (lines 634–647)
From the **stream name**, unless `use_stream_name_as_table_name` is set (it is not here). Transform chain:
1. `stream.replace("-", "_").replace(".", "_")`
2. `camel_to_snake(name, seperate_letter_and_number_in_table_name=True)` (`core.py:1567`) — inserts `_` between camelCase boundaries **and between letters↔digits** (e.g. `foo2` → `foo_2`).
3. collapse repeated `_` → single, strip leading/trailing `_`, `.lower()`.

These stream names are already snake_case, so tables are essentially identical to the stream name: `api_keys`, `messages_usage`, `cost_report`, `claude_code_usage`, `completions_usage`, `costs`, `project_api_keys`, etc. **No dataset prefix/suffix** — dataset comes from the `dataset` config; table = derived name. **Parity gotcha**: the letter↔digit split (`separate_letter_and_number=True` default) — any stream name with an adjacent letter/digit would get an underscore inserted.

## Column mapping — `SchemaTranslator` (`core.py:1129`), `denormalized: true`
Denormalized = **one flat top-level BQ column per top-level JSON-schema property** (`Denormalized.preprocess_record` → `translate_record`, `core.py:960`; contrast fixed-schema mode which wraps everything in one `data` JSON column). Column names run through `transform_column_name`.

**`schema_resolver_version: "2"`** (`_jsonschema_property_to_bigquery_column`, V2 branch lines 1244–1294): far more lenient than V1 — **falls back to `JSON` for anything unresolvable** instead of erroring. Behavior:
- `anyOf` → uses index [0]’s type/format.
- **array**: no `items`/no item `type`/`patternProperties` → `JSON REPEATED`; item type record → `RECORD REPEATED`; else scalar `<type> REPEATED`.
- **object**: no `properties`, empty `properties`, or `patternProperties` present → **`JSON NULLABLE`** (whole object stored as a JSON value); otherwise recurse into a `RECORD` with nested fields (`_translate_record_to_bigquery_schema`, line 1298 — empty props → `JSON`).
- **scalar**: `patternProperties` → `JSON`; else `bigquery_type()`.
- On **any exception** → `JSON NULLABLE` (with a table/field-name special-case in `IGNORE_JSON_FIELDS_FOR_TABLES` → `STRING`).

So nested objects **with a declared schema** become native BQ `RECORD` (STRUCT); schemaless/dynamic objects and arrays-of-unknown become `JSON`; arrays of scalars/records become `REPEATED`. (For these taps most objects are pre-flattened/typed, so expect mostly scalar columns + a few RECORD/JSON.)

**Type map — `bigquery_type` (`core.py:1498`)**: `format:date-time`→`TIMESTAMP`; `date`→`DATE`; `time`→`TIME`; `number`→`FLOAT`; `integer`+`string`→`STRING`; `integer`→`INTEGER`; `boolean`→`BOOLEAN`; `object`→`RECORD`; **else `STRING`** (default/unknown). All scalar fields land `NULLABLE`.

**`column_name_transforms.add_underscore_when_invalid: true`** — `transform_column_name` (`core.py:1524`): strips backticks; removes Unicode whitespace/control/zero-width chars; **if first char is a digit, prepends `_`** (the "add_underscore_when_invalid" behavior); replaces `.`→`_` (`replace_period_with_underscore` is force-set True in translation, lines 1156/1167); and **always** replaces special chars `[!@#$%^&*()/,]`→`_`. Note: `lower`/`snake_case` are **not** enabled by this config, so column casing is preserved as-is from the tap (only the invalid-char/leading-digit fixes apply). The function is `@cache`d.

## `_sdc_` metadata columns — `constants.py:DEFAULT_SCHEMA` / `SDC_FIELDS`; added by `preprocess_record` (`core.py:669`)
Every record gets exactly these 6 system columns popped out and attached (order as emitted). In denormalized mode they sit **alongside** the flat data columns (in fixed mode they accompany the single `data` JSON column):

| Column | BQ type |
|---|---|
| `_sdc_extracted_at` | TIMESTAMP |
| `_sdc_received_at` | TIMESTAMP |
| `_sdc_batched_at` | TIMESTAMP |
| `_sdc_deleted_at` | TIMESTAMP |
| `_sdc_sequence` | INT64 |
| `_sdc_table_version` | INTEGER |

No other system columns (no `_sdc_primary_key`, no `_sdc_received_at`-style extras beyond the above). **For byte-identical tables faucet-sink-bigquery must add these six columns, with these exact names/types, populated with the same semantics** (extracted_at from the tap's record `time_extracted`; received_at/batched_at = target-side timestamps; sequence = ms epoch ordering; deleted_at usually null; table_version usually null for these taps).

## Load method — `batch_job` (`batch_job.py`) + `load_with_retry` (`core.py:1051`)
- **Direct BigQuery load job, no GCS staging** (GCS is a separate `gcs_stage` method). Records are serialized to **newline-delimited JSON** (`orjson.dumps`, `process_record`), buffered and **gzip-compressed in memory** (`Compressor`), then loaded via `client.load_table_from_file(BytesIO(data), …)`.
- `LoadJobConfig` (denormalized, `batch_job.py:139`): `source_format = NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON`, `write_disposition = WRITE_APPEND`, `schema_update_options = [ALLOW_FIELD_ADDITION]`, `ignore_unknown_values = True`, explicit `schema = table.get_resolved_schema()`. One load job per batch (`batch_size`); parallelism via worker pool (`options.max_workers: 1` here → single worker).
- Retries transient job errors up to 3×.

**`overwrite` (WRITE_TRUNCATE full replace) — staging + swap:**
1. On init (`core.py:414`, `_is_overwrite_candidate` supports bool `true` OR fnmatch list), the real table is created (`create_target`), then `self.table` is repointed to a **staging table** `{name}__{YYYYMMDDHHMMSS}__{uuid}` (`_create_overwrite_table`, line 424; expires in `staging_table_expiration_days`, default 3).
2. All batches WRITE_APPEND into staging.
3. `clean_up` (`core.py:872`): a **`WRITE_TRUNCATE` query job** `SELECT * FROM staging` → destination = the real `overwrite_target` (atomic full replace; kept as a query job, not DDL, so it works on partitioned tables). If `key_properties` exist it **dedups**: `QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY <keys> ORDER BY _sdc_extracted_at DESC, _sdc_received_at DESC)=1`. Then drops staging. Optional `overwrite_min_row_ratio` shrink guard can refuse a suspiciously small snapshot.
4. State is **withheld** until the swap completes (`defers_state`, `core.py:742`) so an interrupted run never advances the bookmark past unwritten rows.

**`upsert` (MERGE on key_properties) — staging + MERGE** (`_is_upsert_candidate`, line 448; only when `key_properties` present AND denormalized):
- Staging table receives batches; `merge_table` (`core.py:765`) runs `MERGE target USING staging ON target.<k>=source.<k> (AND … per key) WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET <all matching cols> WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (…)`, then drops staging. Runs in `pre_state_hook` (before each state msg) and `clean_up`. Optional `dedupe_before_upsert` wraps the source in the same QUALIFY dedup.

Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page — what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first — CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world — its materials, instruments, vernacular — is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. The Artifact CSP blocks font CDNs, so don't link a webfont URL and risk a silent fallback. Instead inline the face as a @font-face data URI. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject — the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme, and the viewer has three states, not two: an explicit choice stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, and the default "system" setting stamps *nothing* — most viewers see the un-stamped document, where only `prefers-color-scheme` separates light from dark. Structure the CSS token-level for all three: the bare `:root` block defines the complete light palette (for a deliberately dark-first design, swap light and dark consistently through this whole pattern); `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` redefines only the tokens, guarded as `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` so an explicit light choice beats a dark OS; `:root[data-theme="dark"]` redefines them again so the toggle also wins in the other direction. Style components through the tokens, never directly inside a media or `[data-theme]` block — a color whose only definition sits behind `[data-theme]` never applies in the un-stamped state, and the page renders one theme's text on the other theme's ground. Two more rules keep each theme resolving as a set: the artifact composites over a ground the viewer paints in *its* theme, so `body` must set an explicit `background` from a token — a transparent body silently borrows the host's ground; and every element that sets a color takes it from the same token set as the surface behind it, never a literal that only works in one theme. Before publishing, scan the stylesheet for any color declared only inside a media or `[data-theme]` block — that is the classic unreadable-artifact bug. Give the second theme the same care as the first — don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme — then skip the media query and stamps entirely but still paint the background and every color explicitly, so the page holds on either host ground; make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content — tables, code, diagrams — gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out — a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen — name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it — no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number — a pill, a chip, a severity stripe — so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan — a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles — a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world — headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

**Type** — system grotesk for headings, system sans for body, `ui-monospace` for the data matrix/labels (honest, no blocked-CDN fallback risk); strict scale, tabular figures.
**Layout** — an engineering decision dashboard: thesis + verdict-count band → the sink linchpin callout → a filterable 46-row parity matrix with severity stripes → faucet capability map → blockers → what-to-build → tiered rollout.

Migration analysis · Drivetrain data platform

Replacing the Meltano taps with faucet-stream

Can faucet-stream drop into DrivetrainAi/meltano_taps — 46 sources, all landing in one BigQuery target — and produce the same raw tables? Here is the per-source verdict, and the one thing that gates every row.

Scope: 46 taps · sink: z3z1ma target-bigquery (denormalized, batch_job) · goal: in-place replace, byte-identical BigQuery tables · note: Singer is excluded by design — verdicts use each tap's actual transport (REST / OData / GraphQL / SQL / SOAP / file).

3
Clean source
Reproducible today with a stock connector.
18
With work
Config + faucet transforms / matrix fan-out.
20
Partial
Custom auth, dynamic schema, or some streams blocked.
5
Blocked
Bulk / SDK / SOAP-XLSX / tap↔BigQuery coupling.

⚠ The verdicts above are source-side. Byte-identical tables are gated by the sink — for every row.

The taps all load through one shared target, the z3z1ma target-bigquery fork, in denormalized + batch_job mode. That target does a lot to each table that faucet-sink-bigquery does not do today:

• Auto-creates a denormalized flat schema from the stream's JSON schema (V2 resolver: JSON fallback, RECORD for typed nested, REPEATED arrays). • Adds six _sdc_* system columns to every table — _sdc_extracted_at / received_at / batched_at / deleted_at (TIMESTAMP), _sdc_sequence (INT64), _sdc_table_version (INTEGER). • Applies column-name transforms (leading-digit → _, special chars → _, . → _; no lower-casing). • Month-partitions on _sdc_batched_at and clusters on key_properties[:4]. • Loads gzipped NDJSON load jobs; overwrite = stage → dedup-by-key → WRITE_TRUNCATE swap; upsert = stage → MERGE.

faucet-sink-bigquery today inserts typed columns into a pre-existing table (streaming / MERGE / overwrite-swap, all shipped) but emits no _sdc_ columns, no auto-denormalized schema, no column sanitization, and no month-on-_sdc_batched_at partition/cluster.

Bottom line: a "Singer-compatibility" mode on faucet-sink-bigquery is the single prerequisite for every table to match. Without it, no source is byte-identical; with it, the ~21 green/amber rows below become true drop-in replacements.

01Per-source parity matrix

All 46 taps. Verdict is source-side (transport, auth, fan-out, shaping) assuming the sink-compatibility work above is done. Filter by verdict; the left stripe encodes severity.

SourceMechanismAuthFan-out / streamsVerdictWhat decides it

Verdict key — Clean: stock faucet connector + light config. With work: reproducible via faucet transforms + matrix fan-out/discovery and/or a supported-but-fiddly auth. Partial: custom multi-step auth, per-tenant dynamic schema, or bespoke shaping — approximable with the SQL/WASM transforms but exact parity is hard, or a subset of streams (usually reports) is blocked. Blocked: async bulk, vendor SDK, SOAP-with-embedded-XLSX, or the tap reaches into BigQuery mid-sync — not reproducible by a declarative source→sink pipeline.

02What faucet-stream already covers

Most of the transport, auth and fan-out surface these taps use maps directly onto shipped faucet-stream capabilities — several of them landed in the recent PRs.

Transport

  • REST-JSON — the rest source most taps
  • OData v2/v4 — rest + NextLinkInBody pagination sap · d365 · r365
  • GraphQL — the graphql source shopify
  • SQL warehouse — redshift source redshift
  • Authed CSV / Excel files — rest response_format: csv|excel (#497) sharepoint · onedrive

Auth

  • Bearer / Basic / API-key / custom header ✓
  • OAuth2 client-credentials & refresh, with rotated-token persistence (#499) ✓
  • OAuth1 HMAC-SHA256 (#496) netsuite TBA
  • Mutual TLS client certs (#495) adp
  • Token-endpoint w/ JSONPath token personio envelope

Fan-out & scheduling

  • Static stream matrix + deep merge ✓
  • Parent→child N+1 fan-out pervasive
  • Discovery cross-product (#501) d365-bc · rillet · dualentry
  • Date/period windows — ${now.*} + backfill reports
  • SQL catalog discovery (#211) redshift

Shaping & write

  • flatten · keys_case · select/drop/set/cast · explode ✓
  • SQL / WASM transforms for unpivot, joins, computed cols approximate
  • write_mode: overwrite full-refresh swap (#492) most taps
  • write_mode: upsert + dedup (#224) incremental taps

03The blockers faucet can't reproduce declaratively

These patterns are architectural, not config gaps — they're why the 5 red rows are red and why several "partial" rows lose their report streams.

1Tap ↔ BigQuery coupling

  • netsuite, quickbooks, xero, zohobooks DELETE a rolling window from the destination before re-emitting; sage reads prior BQ output to compute soft-deletes.
  • The tap is a stateful destination mutator. A clean source→sink pipeline never reaches back into the warehouse mid-extract, so these report/incremental streams cannot match.

2Async / bulk / vendor SDK

  • salesforce — Bulk API v1 (create job → poll → download CSV, PK-chunk resume).
  • stripe — official Python SDK + Events-API-as-incremental + async report-run/CSV.
  • Not a paginated-GET pattern; faucet's REST source can't drive the job lifecycle.

3Runtime-synthesized schema

  • hubspot builds stream classes at runtime for custom objects/associations/history + a 10k-result id workaround.
  • Per-tenant dynamic columns: bamboohr custom reports, hibob metadata, personio, ukg UDFs, campfire custom fields.

4Bespoke report shaping

  • rillet hand-flattens a hierarchical report tree with reconciliation rules + elimination-entity unions.
  • quickbooks / xero flatten a Rows/Columns matrix; oracle_fusion parses a base64 XLSX out of a SOAP body.

5Multi-step / signed auth

  • bullhorn refresh→access→login→BhRestToken + dynamic base URL; sap, acumatica cookie-session login; sage session pool; skyslope HMAC + session.
  • faucet's auth providers are single-step; these need a session/pre-flight provider.

6Exact record-shape fidelity

  • Every tap flattens to parent_child columns and JSON-stringifies nested fields with a specific delimiter/rule set.
  • "Same table" means matching that column set and the six _sdc_ columns exactly — reproducible, but it's per-tap transform work, not free.

04What to build for full parity

In priority order. Item 1 unblocks every row; the rest expand how many taps reach true drop-in status.

  1. faucet-sink-bigquery "Singer-compat" mode — prerequisite for all 46

    Auto-denormalized schema from inferred JSON schema (V2 rules), the six _sdc_* columns with matching semantics, z3z1ma column-name transforms, month-partition on _sdc_batched_at + cluster on keys, and gzipped-NDJSON load jobs with staged overwrite-dedup / MERGE. Nothing is byte-identical without this.

  2. Session / pre-flight auth provider — unlocks bullhorn · sap · acumatica · sage · skyslope

    A shared provider that runs a login step, captures a token/cookie/dynamic base-URL, and re-authenticates on 401 — modelled like the existing oauth2_refresh provider.

  3. Bookmark → request-parameter injection — server-side incremental

    Let the stored bookmark flow into a query param / filter (Lucene range, gte|, OData $filter, If-Modified-Since). Today faucet filters incremental client-side.

  4. Report/matrix flattening recipes — rillet · qbo · xero reports

    Ship SQL/WASM transform templates for report-tree and Rows/Columns-matrix flattening. Still can't match streams that also delete-from-BigQuery.

  5. Async-job source pattern — salesforce bulk · stripe reports

    A source shape that submits a job, polls, and downloads the result (CSV). Larger effort; only two taps need it.

05Suggested rollout

Once the sink-compat mode exists, migrate in waves of decreasing determinism.

Wave 1 Clean & with-work

21 taps — stock connector + config/transforms, mostly full-refresh overwrite (easiest to prove identical).

  • ramp, brex, invoiced, redshift, netsuite_pro, ms365fno, ms365bc, afas, dualentry, deskera, restaurant365, campfire, adp, isolved, paylocity, rippling, greenhouse, lever, navan, anthropic, openai

Wave 2 Partial

20 taps — need a session-auth provider, dynamic-schema handling, or per-tap shaping recipes; validate table-by-table.

  • sap, syteline, acumatica, sharepointsites, onedrive, shopify, plaid, bamboohr, hibob, personio, ukg_pro, deel, bullhorn, skyslope, attio, quickbooks*, xero*, zohobooks*, sage*, rillet* (*entity streams only; report streams blocked)

Hold Blocked

5 taps — keep on Meltano until the async-job / session patterns land, or accept a non-identical rebuild.

  • salesforce (bulk API), stripe (SDK + events + reports), netsuite (SuiteQL + BQ mutation), hubspot (runtime streams + BQ side-channel), oracle_fusion (SOAP + XLSX)

"Blocked" means not reproducible by a declarative source→sink pipeline without new faucet capabilities, not that the source is unreachable.

Here's how your three points reshaped it:

**1. `_sdc_` columns ignored** — and that collapses the sink concern. faucet-sink-bigquery already loads via BigQuery load jobs (`CREATE_IF_NEEDED`), does the overwrite = staged truncate-swap, MERGE upsert, and schema-evolution. Column-name transforms via inbuilt features** — yes. `flatten` → `parent_child`, `keys_case` → snake_case, `rename_keys`/`rename_field` for aliases, `set` for injected columns, `cast` for epoch↔timestamp. So naming/flattening stop being blockers, which is why the "Supported" set jumped from 3 → **20**. One gap: JSON-stringifying a nested field has no inbuilt transform, so it currently falls to SQL — I flagged a one-line `json_encode` transform (build item #3) that would keep those rows inbuilt-only.

**3. SQL counts (flagged), WASM doesn't.** New scoring — **20 Supported / 10 Needs-SQL / 12 Partial / 4 Blocked** (30 of 46 reachable with connectors + inbuilt/SQL transforms). §02 lists exactly **what SQL unlocks**: wide→long unpivot (deel, sharepoint/onedrive timeseries, personio), reference-table joins (hibob labels, anthropic pricing, bamboohr aliases), report-tree/matrix flatten (rillet, qbo/xero, attio, ukg cross-join). §03 lists the **only WASM-territory case** — `oracle_fusion`'s base64-XLSX-inside-SOAP decode, which SQL can't express, so it stays Blocked and uncounted.

Key honest takeaway: with your rules, **the remaining non-green rows are not shaping problems** — they're auth (session-login / custom HMAC: sap, acumatica, bullhorn, syteline, sage, skyslope), transport (bulk/SDK: salesforce, stripe; SOAP-XLSX: oracle_fusion), runtime stream synthesis (hubspot), or report streams coupled to a mid-sync BigQuery `DELETE` (quickbooks/xero/zohobooks/sage). SQL and WASM don't fix those — an auth provider, an async-job source, and report-decoupling do (build list §04).

**On `_faucet_*` columns — good idea, filed it: #510.** An opt-in sink decorator stamping `_faucet_extracted_at` / `_faucet_loaded_at` / `_faucet_run_id` / `_faucet_source`. Not needed for parity (since you dropped `_sdc`), but genuinely useful for freshness/lineage/incident triage without coupling the connector to the destination — which is exactly the anti-pattern that blocks the accounting taps. I scoped it as a connector-agnostic decorator (like the cleanup tracker) so every sink benefits.

Okay, now think about what all things can be structurally added. It should not be a hacky thing just to support one connector. It should be something which is a first-class citizen, a real feature, a real addition to the base framework, which will unbox not just this but multiple other things which will be of a similar type. What are first-class features that you think we can add which can unblock or move from partial to total, won't need SQL, or something like that, and make the job easy?

Great framing — the test is "does it unlock a *class*, not a connector." I went back through all 46 taps and clustered the non-green rows by their *root cause*, not their vendor. Seven root causes cover essentially everything, and each maps to one real framework primitive. Here they are, ordered by leverage.

## 1. A composable auth-flow provider *(the single biggest unlock)*
Today `AuthProvider` is single-step (bearer / oauth2 / oauth2_refresh / oauth1 / token-endpoint). The recurring wall is **auth that is a small program**: log in, capture something, place it somewhere, maybe sign each request.

Make auth a **declarative flow** with four composable pieces:
- **pre-flight chain** — run request(s), extract token / cookie / *dynamic base-URL* via JSONPath (`bullhorn` refresh→access→login→`BhRestToken`+`restUrl`; `sap`/`acumatica` cookie login; `sage` session; `personio` `/v1/auth` envelope).
- **credential placement** — header / query / **body** / cookie, via a template (`plaid` creds-in-body, `afas` `AfasToken`, `zoho` `Zoho-oauthtoken`, `ukg` dual header, `campfire` `Token `).
- **pluggable request signer** — a signing hook (`skyslope` custom HMAC; and it generalizes to AWS SigV4, Azure SAS later).
- **refresh + rotation + single-flight** — already have the bones (#499).

**Unlocks / hardens:** sap, acumatica, bullhorn, sage, syteline, skyslope → out of Partial; plus cleaner plaid/afas/zoho/ukg/campfire/personio/netsuite. Auth is universal, so this is the least "hacky" thing on the list.

## 2. A first-class OData source
Six taps are OData that we're currently hand-rolling on `rest` (`sap`, `ms365bc`, `ms365fno`, `netsuite_pro`, `restaurant365`, `acumatica`). OData is a *standard* — a dedicated source handles `@odata.nextLink`, `$filter`/`$orderby`/`$expand`, the `{value}` unwrap (acumatica), and `$metadata` (EDMX) → schema/stream discovery, once. It turns "6 fiddly configs + notes" into "6 clean rows," and every future OData ERP is free.

## 3. Server-side incremental push-down (state → request binding)
faucet tracks bookmarks but filters **client-side**. ~15 taps push the bookmark into the request (`greenhouse` `gte|`, OData `$filter ge`, `bullhorn` Lucene range, `xero` `If-Modified-Since` header, `ms365*` `SysModified`, `netsuite` `lastmodifieddate`, `shopify` query DSL…). Add a small **binding spec**: "render the stored bookmark into `{query param | header | body field | path}` with this operator template; advance from this response field." Generalizes to *every* incremental API and fixes row-count parity + cost.

## 4. An async-job source pattern (submit → poll → fetch)
A whole class of "big data" APIs is submit-a-job / poll-status / download-result: `salesforce` Bulk, `stripe` reports, plus (future) Amplitude/Mixpanel/Google-Ads/warehouse-unload exports. A first-class 3-phase source (submit → poll on a status JSONPath with terminal states → fetch result URL) turns two Blocked rows into Supported and is a reusable primitive for dozens of connectors we don't have yet.

## 5. A response-decode pipeline on sources
Right now the body must be JSON (or, via #497, a CSV/Excel file). Make decoding a **declarative chain**: extract a field (JSONPath) → base64-decode → gunzip/unzip → parse (json / csv / xlsx / xml). That unlocks `oracle_fusion` (base64-XLSX-in-SOAP — the *only* WASM-territory case today), and it's exactly what bulk/report results need (they're usually zipped CSV). Pairs with #4.

## 6. Three inbuilt reshape transforms — to delete the SQL dependency
You want fewer SQL rows. Almost every "Needs SQL" case is one of three shapes:
- **`unpivot`** (map / wide → long): `deel` gross-to-net, `attio` value-map, `personio` pivot, `sharepoint` timeseries.
- **`lookup` / `enrich`** (join a small reference set fetched once → add label columns): `hibob` named-lists, `anthropic` pricing, `bamboohr` field aliases. (Reuses the #501 discovery machinery as the reference source.)
- **`json_encode`** (stringify a nested field): the ubiquitous one.

Ship these three inbuilt and **the "Needs SQL" column basically empties** — only genuinely bespoke arithmetic would remain, and even that (anthropic pricing) becomes `lookup` + `set`.

## 7. Self-describing stream/schema discovery
Generalize #211 (DB catalog) + #501 (value discovery) into **"discover streams + schemas from a metadata endpoint"**: OData `$metadata`, `afas` `/metainfo`, `hubspot` `/schemas` custom objects, `bamboohr`/`personio`/`ukg` report+UDF metadata, `sharepoint`'s per-file manifest. This is the primitive behind hubspot's "runtime-synthesized streams" done declaratively — the API describes itself, we generate the matrix.

---

**Bonus (sink side): scoped/windowed overwrite.** The accounting taps (`quickbooks`/`xero`/`zohobooks`/`sage` reports, and `hubspot`) reach *into* BigQuery to `DELETE` a rolling window before re-appending. Add a **`write_mode: overwrite` scoped to a window/key** ("replace only rows matching this run's scope") — the same idea as #478 scoped cleanup, applied to writes. That removes the tap↔warehouse coupling entirely and is a real primitive for any rolling-window/report load.

## Net effect
These 7 (+1) are orthogonal primitives, not patches. Together they'd move the fleet from **~30/46 reachable to ~44/46 Supported**, and #6 alone **eliminates almost all SQL**. The only genuine residual is truly one-off logic (very rare). Sequencing by leverage: **#1 auth-flow → #6 reshape transforms → #3 incremental push-down → #2 OData source → #4+#5 async-job+decode → #7 discovery → scoped overwrite.**

Want me to file these as tracked epics on `faucet-hq/faucet-stream` (cross-linked to the roadmap #38), and add a "first-class primitives" section to the artifact? I'd file #1, #3, and #6 as the top-priority trio since they unblock the most with the least surface area.
Yes, please file this. I am 100% sure, right? These are first-class features that we are adding, and not just some hacks that we are opening up.
On it — filing all seven (plus the scoped-overwrite sink primitive) as first-class feature epics on `faucet-hq/faucet-stream`, cross-linked to the roadmap. Let me write the bodies and create them.
